newsitem.title: GERMANY: German court rejects tobacco firms' plea on warning.
newsitem.headline: German court rejects tobacco firms' plea on warning.

text.p: Germany's highest court on Wednesday rejected a bid by tobacco firms to declare illegal health warnings on cigarette packets which link smoking to cancer and other serious illness.

The Federal Constitutional Court in Karlsruhe dismissed claims by the firms -- Reemtsma, Rothaendle, Austria Tabak GmbH and Nestor Gianaclis -- that the warnings infringed several of their basic rights.
German cigarette packets have carried the warnings -- "smoking causes cancer" and "smoking causes heart and circulatory diseases" -- since 1991 as the result of a European Union directive.
The companies argued that placing these warnings on their packets gave the impression smoking always led to cancer, when in fact smoking was only one of several risk factors.

The court rejected the firms' claim that the warnings infringed their freedom to express an opinion and their freedom to carry out their job. Warning the population of health risks was a legitimate task of the state, the court said.
